bandsNote: Hidden from students. Band rises only by getting items right; never named on screen.
hintRule: Hint 1 points to the step card. Hint 2 does the first step. Hint 3 shows the same move on a different example. No hint gives the answer. Each hint costs a fresh attempt before the next opens.

items.prompt: This flame is yellow-orange. Which known metal does it match?
hints: Open your table. Find the row whose color says yellow-orange.
Read down the color column until you see yellow-orange. What metal is in that row?
Another case: a blue-green flame matches the row that says blue-green. Do the same with yellow-orange.

items.prompt: This flame is orange-red. Which known metal does it match?
hints: Use your table, not memory.
Find the row that says orange-red.
Compare the swatch with each color in your table. Which swatch is the same?

items.prompt: NaCl and NaNO3 both burn yellow-orange. What sets the flame color?
hints: Look at what NaCl and NaNO3 have in common.
The two salts have different second parts. What is the same in both?
Another case: the same red paint on a door and on a wall. The color comes from the paint, not from the thing it covers. Which part of each salt plays the role of the paint?

items.prompt: A student says the chlorine in NaCl makes the yellow color. Which result in your table shows this is wrong?
options: NaNO3 has no chlorine and is also yellow-orange
items.answer: NaNO3 has no chlorine and is also yellow-orange
hints: The student's claim is about chlorine. Which test has no chlorine?
Find the salt in your table that lacks Cl.
To test a claim about one part, change only that part and see whether the result changes.

items.prompt: You see a lilac flame. Which metal is it, and why might yellow hide it?
options: K; sodium's bright yellow can mask it
Cu; the yellow is the splint
items.answer: K; sodium's bright yellow can mask it
hints: Look up lilac in your table.
Now look at how bright sodium is compared with that metal.
Another case: a dim light next to a very bright one is hard to see. Which flame is the dim light here?

items.prompt: The flame shows a yellow flash, then lilac. Which metal are you burning?
options: K, with a little sodium on the splint
items.answer: K, with a little sodium on the splint
hints: Which color lasted?
The color that lasts is the metal. The flash is something extra.
Another case: a quick yellow flash from a splint is sodium, not your sample.

items.prompt: Which two metals could you mix up if you used only your eyes?
hints: Look for two rows with the same color name.
Read the color column again. Which two match?
Rows with identical swatches look identical. Find the identical swatches.

items.prompt: A spectroscope shows one yellow line at 589 nm. Which metal?
hints: Find the yellow region of the strip.
Which metal's row has a line at the yellow position?
Another case: a blue line near 461 nm points to the row that has a blue line. Do the same with yellow.

items.prompt: An unknown burns crimson. Your knowns include Li and Sr, both crimson. Which claim is true to the data?
options: It is Li or Sr; a second test is needed.
items.answer: It is Li or Sr; a second test is needed.
hints: How many known metals match crimson?
If two metals match, can the color alone choose between them?
Another case: two keys fit the same lock. The lock alone cannot tell you which key you hold.

items.prompt: A spectroscope shows a bright red line near 671 nm and a dimmer orange line near 610 nm. There is no blue line. Which metal?
hints: Check each row of the strip for a blue line.
Which of Li and Sr has a blue line?
Another case: Na has one yellow line and no blue line. Decide the same way for these two.

items.prompt: A spectroscope shows a blue line near 461 nm plus red lines. Which metal?
hints: Find the blue region of the strip.
Which crimson metal has a blue line?
The blue line is the difference between the two crimson metals.

items.prompt: In one sentence: what can the flame test not decide?
items.grading: PENDING (decision for Ian): self-compare with the model answer, or you read it
items.modelAnswer: It cannot separate metals that burn the same color, such as Li and Sr.
hints: Think about the Li and Sr rows.
Finish: The flame cannot decide between metals that ___.
Another case: two shirts of the same color cannot be told apart by color.
